recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. If the AllergyIntolerance narrative's ruled-out/high-certainty wording should be broadened to match the terminology definition, handle that as a separate Patient Care review of the later FHIR-28458 guidance rather than as FHIR-15024 reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-15024 was a Published Patient Care change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking that the AllergyIntoleranceVerificationStatus code system not define refuted as simply disproven/refuted and instead say the assertion has been disputed or disproven with sufficient clinical certainty to invalidate it.
initial_application: Git commit 6fa90a868c applied GF#15024 by updating source/allergyintolerance/allergyintolerance-spreadsheet.xml from the old disproven/high-certainty wording to the approved disputed-or-disproven definition. Historical R4/R4B release artifacts contain that applied wording.
additional_context: Current core no longer owns the AllergyIntoleranceVerificationStatus CodeSystem source after terminology content moved out of core; source/allergyintolerance/valueset-allergyintolerance-verification.xml includes http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/allergyintolerance-verification. The active AllergyIntolerance narrative still says refuted allergies indicate a reaction has been ruled out with high clinical certainty, but later Published issue FHIR-28458 explicitly added or preserved that guidance while addressing clinicalStatus for refuted records.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The seed's requested code-system definition is already reflected in the terminology artifact consumed by core, and changing the later AllergyIntolerance narrative under this seed would overrun a separate Patient Care decision.
